newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Big rise for Bank/Scotland profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Big rise for Bank/Scotland profits.

text.p: Analysts expect Bank of Scotland, which reports first half figures next Wednesday, to post a big rise in pre-tax profits but point out the results will not really be comparable with the first half of last year.

This is because the numbers will include a contribution from BankWest, Bank of Scotland's Australian unit. Michael Lever, banking analyst at HSBC James Capel, said he expects profits before tax of over 300 million stg, saying that the figures are likely to come out near the top of the market range of 288 to 310 million stg.
Profits before tax were 262 million stg in the first half of last year. Lever expects Bank of Scotland to raise its interim dividend payout by 16 percent to 2.85p.
Analysts expect some margin pressure to show through the figures but this will have been largely offset by Bank of Scotland's move into more consumer-oriented business.
The bank's cost to income ratio is likely to deteriorate but this should come as no surprise to the market as higher spending on its branch network and infrastructure have been well flagged.
"The feature is likely to be very strong income growth based on strong volumes," Lever said.

Analysts say bank of Scotland is unlikely to present any clues on its strategy. Nobody expects it to make further major acquisitions in the near-term, as it is short of capital after its BankWest deal. The sale by Standard Life of most of its 32.2 percent stake in Bank of Scotalnd earlier this year removed one source of speculation surrounding the bank. But, few analysts seriously considered the possibility this bastion of the Scottish establishment would be allowed to fall into "foreign" control. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
